decisions.label: Wiki-faithful Markdown corpus
decisions.detail: Real wikitext (not flattened plain text) parsed with mwparserfromhell and converted to Markdown — headings, bold/italic, links, lists, and tables preserved; citation clutter dropped. 24-60% more corpus text per language than v1, and full of highly-repetitive structural symbols (**, ##, |) that compress extremely well.

decisions.label: Metaspace pre-tokenizer
decisions.detail: Keeps punctuation attached to its word ("India," stays one unit) instead of splitting it off — this is what lets a single learned token cover more than one "faithful unit", the mechanism that pushes fertility below 1.0.

decisions.label: NFKC normalizer, no Lowercase
decisions.detail: NFKC collapses Unicode compatibility variants (ﬁ → fi, fullwidth forms, etc.). Lowercase was tried and tested but dropped once found to be a strict downgrade here: NFKC-only beat NFKC+Lowercase on both score (16,581 vs 13,458) and round-trip fidelity — unlike v1, where Lowercase is a real, unambiguous win.

decisions.label: Explicit [UNK] token
decisions.detail: Same as v1 — an unrecognized character becomes a real, visible, counted [UNK] token.

decisions.label: Metaspace decoder
decisions.detail: Makes decode(encode(text)) genuinely invertible: the replacement character (▁) marks exactly where a real space was, so decoding can reconstruct it — verified exact round-trip on normal text, including multi-token words and attached punctuation.

decisions.label: Same 3-group merge strategy as v1
decisions.detail: English alone, Telugu alone, Hindi+Marathi trained jointly (they share Devanagari) — same reasoning as v1.

decisions.label: Symmetric equalization (no English carve-out)
decisions.detail: Unlike v1, English no longer needs special protection — the richer corpus + Metaspace + NFKC combo gets every language comfortably under the fertility target on its own. So the full 10,000-token budget is split to equalize all three groups as tightly as possible, English included.

decisions.label: Fertility metric: "faithful units"
decisions.detail: tokens / faithful_units, computed over the whole running corpus (not per-unique-word like v1). A faithful_unit is one contiguous letter/mark/number run, or one punctuation/symbol character counted individually. Because it's occurrence-weighted, common short words and punctuation dominate the average — this is why fertility can drop below 1.0 here but couldn't in v1.

cons.label: OOV characters still break exact round-trip
cons.detail: An unrecognized character decodes back as the literal 5-character string "[UNK]", not the original character — inherent to having any UNK token at all, not fixable without full byte-level coverage.

cons.label: Markdown/table conversion is best-effort
cons.detail: Wikitext tables and infobox parameters are flattened into plain value lists rather than perfectly reconstructed — not pixel-perfect, though it captures far more real content than v1's plain-text extraction.
